items.method: Cross-read cash-market breadth (share of constituents positive versus the 60% broad-participation threshold) against the single-name options tape (call-versus-put premium, call fraction and the strike and days-to-expiry of the heaviest same-session prints), the dealer-positioning corridor (positive dealer gamma, flip, put and call walls, front expected move, pin-to-maxpain playbook) and the intraday auction state, then judge whether put-heavy premium meeting a long-gamma pin now sits over a repaired internal that confirms the grind or a deteriorating one that would let the pin fail, and anchor a direction-correct invalidation BELOW the benchmark at the flip-and-put-wall loss that would falsify the constructive lean.
items.note: The genuinely new configuration this window is that cash participation has crossed back above the broad line while the derivative tape stays defensive, so the internal signal and the hedging signal now point opposite ways rather than reinforcing a downside read. Market-heatmap breadth is 60.22% of 134 constituents positive, a 0.22-point cushion over the 60% broad-participation threshold — a reclaim of the line that was missed by 0.14 points in the prior window. Single-name option premium is nonetheless still outright put-heavy: a 0.381 call fraction, $1.827B of call premium against $2.968B of put premium across 12 tickers, with 1964 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days (626 of 19158 considered). The heaviest near-dated prints are defensive — an IWM 290 put at $17.0M on 34.8x its open interest fourteen days out, a QQQ 720 put at $106.8M on 34.5x open interest zero days out and an NVDA 225 put at $147.3M on 6.76x open interest zero days out. That hedging lands on a positive dealer-gamma structure: SPY reads positive gamma with the flip near 768.84, put wall 768 and call wall 770 inside a plus-or-minus 3.26 front expected move, signed net GEX about +0.35B, and the gamma playbook is pin-to-maxpain with a patient, same-session-fade hold. The most recent intraday auction is a Trend day · down under Mixed control (VWAP 770.95, +0.09% gap, 79 bars). With breadth now above the line and the benchmark carried near 771.1 above the 770 call wall, the read leans modestly constructive: the put-heavy premium looks like hedging being absorbed by a long-gamma grind that internals now confirm, rather than downside leadership. The confirming trigger for the constructive case is the benchmark holding above the 768.84 flip and 770 call wall while breadth stays above 60%; the constructive lean is invalidated on a daily close below ~767.50 on SPY, which loses the 768 put wall and the 768.84 gamma flip, would flip dealers toward selling weakness and would show the put premium was leading the tape rather than hedging a grind.
items.title: Breadth has reclaimed the 60% participation line (60.22% of 134 constituents) beneath the same put-heavy option tape and positive-gamma pin that pressured the prior window — SPY dealers are long gamma with the flip at 768.84 and walls 768/770 inside a plus-or-minus 3.26 expected move, single-name premium is still put-heavy at a 0.381 call fraction ($1.827B calls vs $2.968B puts across 12 names, 1964 contracts clearing the $250k bar), and the heaviest prints are an IWM 290 put at $17.0M on 34.8x open interest, a QQQ 720 put at $106.8M and an NVDA 225 put at $147.3M zero days out, while the intraday auction still reads Trend day · down at VWAP 770.95

items.method: Cross-read the steadying US internals (breadth reclaiming the participation line, put-heavy single-name premium, a down-trend intraday auction) against where leadership is actually being scored — the global-rotation composite (Singapore, Taiwan, Canada ahead of the US-heavy ACWI) and the real-assets 0-100 composite (crypto and broad commodities leading, gold firmer but rate-shadowed, silver weak, oil middling) — to test whether risk appetite is sitting offshore and in real assets while the domestic tape firms, then, finding the leadership cluster resolves to relative-strength scores and composite rankings rather than any single committed-universe price level, withhold a tactical call rather than publish one that cannot be scored.
items.note: The second cross-model pattern this window is that the leadership scores keep pointing away from the domestic tape even as US internals firm, so the migration remains a where-is-the-bid observation rather than a confirmation of index direction. The US picture has steadied: market-heatmap breadth has reclaimed the line at 60.22% of 134 constituents, single-name option premium is put-heavy at a 0.381 call fraction ($2.968B puts versus $1.827B calls), and the intraday auction is a Trend day · down under Mixed control at VWAP 770.95. Against that, global rotation ranks EWS (Singapore) first at 87.7/100 versus the US-heavy ACWI, with EWT (Taiwan) 77.8, EWC (Canada) 73.9 and EWG (Germany) 68.5 ahead of a middling US read, and the Singapore leg is a mixed, local-equity-led move with an FX drag rather than a dollar tailwind. Real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities — ETH-USD 77.5, bitcoin (BTC-USD) 70, IBIT 66.7, PDBC 66.6 (six-month momentum +25.14%), DBC 66.4 (+22.67%) and agriculture DBA 66 — while the monetary metals split: gold (GLD) is firmer at 48.5 in an uptrend but still carries six-month momentum of -11.49%, and silver (SLV) 22.5 stays mixed at -21.98%; oil (USO) 53.9 sits in the middle on a flat -0.59% three-month pulse. Offshore-equity and speculative real-asset leadership with a rate-shadowed gold and weak silver, set against a defensive US sector rotation that rotates into materials (XLB Leading, accel +3.4) with healthcare the named leader (XLV, accel +1.08) as technology rolls over from a peak (XLK Peaking, accel -1.57), is a where-is-the-bid observation, not a scoreable trade: the cluster resolves to relative-strength states and 0-100 composite scores, none of which is a single committed-universe instrument with a direction-correct price trigger this window, so a tactical call is withheld rather than published with only a working side. Watch whether US breadth holds above the 60% participation line to close the gap with the offshore and real-asset leadership, or whether the down-trend domestic tape drags the composite reads lower; until an instrument-level price trigger is in view, the cluster is carried as counter-weight context to the index-level constructive lean, not as its own call.
items.title: Leadership still sits offshore and in speculative real assets while US internals steady — global rotation ranks Singapore (EWS 87.7), Taiwan (EWT 77.8) and Canada (EWC 73.9) ahead of the US-heavy ACWI, and real assets are led by crypto and broad commodities (ETH-USD 77.5, BTC-USD 70, IBIT 66.7, PDBC 66.6, DBC 66.4) with gold (GLD 48.5, six-month momentum -11.49%) firmer but rate-shadowed, silver (SLV 22.5, -21.98%) weak and oil (USO 53.9) middling, a cross-model migration that resolves to no single committed-universe price level
